Findings, all MEASURED: (1) `signals/fusion/lifecycle.py::_latest_price` full-scanned `evidence_dots` (422k rows, 95ms, no symbol index) once per open episode — 2,207 open episodes = ~200 CPU-s per pass on a 60s cadence, i.e. one thread pinned at ~100% all session; (2) `db/idea_outcomes.update_outcome` re-ran `init_idea_outcomes_tables` (33 `PRAGMA table_info` round-trips, ~2ms) on EVERY write and the idea sweep writes ~8.5k rows per pass (the forming daily close changes each pass); (3) `db/fusion.init_fusion_tables` (0.9ms) is called by 17 accessors and the fusion intake calls several per event at 24 events/s. Fixed: `idx_evidence_symbol_ts ON evidence_dots(symbol, ts, id)` (31ms→3µs per lookup, created on boot by `init_fusion_tables`); `db/schema_helpers.once_per_db` — a decorator memoising `init_<x>_tables` per (path, inode) per process, applied to the two hot modules (a DB deleted and recreated at the same path re-runs the DDL; two tests that replayed a migration in-process now clear the memo to simulate the fresh process a legacy DB actually meets); the lifecycle loop shares one read connection instead of opening one per episode. Result: process CPU ~215% → ~106% of a core at steady state; under a 10-request concurrent burst `/api/snapshot` 0.5s (was 5–10s), `/api/watchlist/market` 0.7–1.5s (was 13.6s), bars ≤0.9s. Full suite 4,290 passed. Left on the table, recorded not hidden: the fusion intake is now the biggest consumer (~25–35% of a core) — 85k dispositions/hour of which 87% are `shed`/`ignored_by_rule`, and each discarded event still pays its own connection + INSERT + commit AND a `set_cursor` commit (~50 fsyncs/s of bookkeeping); batching discards per store per pass in one transaction is the obvious fix but it is inside the Decision Engine's intake and gets its own reviewed round. | 2026-08-17 | **Candles gapping off the prior close again — the skipped-bucket rollover now opens at `prev.close` like every other rollover (`frontend/lib/chart-engine/merge.ts`).** Founder: "candles aren't lining up" after the morning's phantom-wick fix. Checked first whether that fix could do it: `use-symbol-quote` only withholds a stale price across a symbol switch, so no. Real cause is two 08-1x changes stacking: #307 (08-12) made a rollover whose tail is ≥2 buckets behind open at the **live price** ("the gap is the truth" — written for FXE, where a missing minute means nothing traded), and #308 (08-13) added serve-stale bars so a first payload can be up to ~11 min old. Measured today, replaying the chart's exact `steps` math against `/api/bars` + `/ws/market`: on **liquid** names the 1Min tail sits **137–197s** behind at load (SPY steps=3, TSLA steps=2 on one run; steps=1 on a run 3 min later — a coin flip per load), and the **5Min** vendor series never contains the forming bucket (tail = 15:40 at 15:48), so any load in the back half of a 5-min window also lands on steps=2. That branch drew vendor lag as a price jump on most loads, and the bar then survives refreshes (`mergeFetchedBars` keeps the local tail) so the gap sits there until the vendor bucket arrives. Fix: `rolledOverBar` opens at `prev.close` unconditionally; the `steps` placement (bucket containing now, skipped ones left for the refetch) is unchanged. On a thin symbol this now draws a temporary wick across the dead time instead of a temporary gap — both are overwritten by the vendor bar within a refresh, and the wick is the honest shape on the names actually charted. Test flipped to pin the new contract (15/15 green), `tsc` + eslint clean on the touched lines. Deployed; pending in-browser check. |
| 2026-08-17 | **Phantom candle wicks fixed — the chart was painting the PREVIOUS symbol's live price onto the new symbol's forming bar (`frontend/lib/use-symbol-quote.ts`).** Founder saw a wick to ~$406-407 on TSLA (~$340) across 1Day/1Hour/5Min, and earlier on another ticker. Diagnosis by measurement, not guess: `/api/bars` for TSLA was clean on every timeframe (today's vendor high 345.05), the live `/ws/market` stream for TSLA was clean (all frames 340.2x, no held/admitted suspect-print log lines for TSLA all day — the backend ±3% trade guard never even fired), so the 406 came from the frontend. The backend request log showed GLD was charted just before TSLA, and GLD's session range today was 400.77–406.16 with last 405.75 — the wick IS GLD's price. Mechanism: `useSymbolQuote` keeps `price` in React state; on a symbol switch the effect opens a NEW socket for the new symbol but the state still holds the OLD symbol's price until the first frame arrives (a network round-trip), while `native-chart`'s fetch resolves from the client bars cache in a microtask — so its live-merge effect ran with `livePrice`=GLD against TSLA's freshly-set bars, and 406/340 = +19% sails under the chart's ±50% plausibility band. Channel-linked workspaces have several chart widgets (one per timeframe) each with its own hook instance, which is exactly why every timeframe got the wick at once; the same stale value also flashed in the widget-header price. Fix (19 lines): tag the stored quote with the symbol it belongs to and return `undefined` for price/ext/session until the tag matches the requested symbol — race-free by construction rather than by reset-ordering. The wick self-heals once a fresh vendor payload lands (vendor bars always win in `mergeFetchedBars`), which is why it appeared and lingered for a cache TTL rather than forever. Not changed: the ±50% band (deliberately loose for real gaps); no hook test added — the frontend has no React testing-library. `npm run typecheck` + eslint clean; pending in-browser check after deploy. |

Policy recorded in memory `firecrawl-local-reader`. | 2026-08-12 | **The chart's staleness gate threw live ticks away instead of moving the bar forward — and on a thin symbol it never let go (#307).** The follow-up #306 named, taken next at the founder's call. **It also corrects a claim I recorded there as fact.** #306's row asserts the gate is "effectively half-on for every 1-minute chart… the vendor tail is chronically ~2 intervals old, so the live merge is blocked and no tick ever walks the previous close forward." That was **reasoned, not measured, and wrong in shape** — house rule is that any claim about system state written down as fact gets verified against live state, and this one wasn't. Replaying the effect against the real tick stream (faithful to the 60s bars cache, the 30s refresh, object-identity early-return, `mergeFetchedBars`, the gate, the 300s cooldown and rollover) shows the truth is **bistable, not chronic**: once a rollover has fired, the locally-formed bar IS the current bucket and survives every refresh (`mergeFetchedBars` keeps local bars past the payload's end), so the tail is never stale and the gate is **literally unreachable** — run A, SPY, **0 of 1,400 ticks blocked**. But the gate blocks the very rollover that starts that loop, so a load whose *first* payload is already ≥2 intervals old never enters it — run B, same symbol, same code, **427 of 1,400 ticks dropped, 91s of 300s with a frozen chart**. A coin flip at page load, which is why it reads as intermittent. ★ **The threshold sits below our own worst case**: served tail age = Alpaca's publish lag (~60–78s, a minute bar exists only after the minute closes) **+ up to the full 60s bars cache** = **137s measured**, against a `2 × interval` = **120s** gate on 1Min. It was never a margin. **And thin symbols never recover, because there is no fresher bar to fetch** — a minute with no trades produces no bar at all: measured over 5 RTH days, **FXE has 69.5% of consecutive minute bars ≥2 intervals apart** (median gap 180s, max 40 min) and dropped **10 of 10** ticks behind a 42-minute-stale tail, PSQ 7.5%, IBB 1.8%, while SPY/TSLA/AAPL/NVDA/GLD/SLV and /ES are all **0.0%** — so the defect is invisible on exactly the names anyone tests with. **Root cause of the block was `engine.rollover` being single-step**: it could only produce `last.time + interval`, so merging a tail more than one bucket behind would have stamped the live price into a bucket that already closed — the gate existed to keep single-step safe, and the two were a matched pair. Fix removes the pairing rather than loosening the number: **count buckets instead of testing staleness.** `steps = floor((now − last) / interval)`; `rollover(intervalMs, price, steps)` appends **exactly one** bar at `last.time + steps × interval` — the bucket containing *now* — and never fabricates the skipped ones. The open is decided by contiguity: `steps === 1` opens at `prev.close` (the #306 fix — the tape ran continuously and the apparent gap was only the stale snapshot), `steps > 1` opens at **`price`**, because bars are genuinely absent between the two and on a thin name **nothing traded in between, so the gap IS the honest rendering** and the bucket's first print is its open. The ≥2 test survives, now doing only what it was for: kicking a refetch. It no longer returns. **Verified by replaying the patched logic on live ticks, not by argument:** FXE 10/10 dropped → **0 dropped** (4 applyLive + 6 rollovers + 1 refetch kick, then self-sustaining), SPY 1,161 ticks **0 dropped**, with in-replay assertions that timestamps stay unique and ascending and that every rolled bar lands in the bucket containing now — both held throughout. 85 frontend tests green (3 new pinning multi-step placement, the skipped-bucket open, and `steps=1` ≡ default), `tsc --noEmit` + `check:tokens` clean, `ruff` clean repo-wide. That cap started as a bound on each individual *sleep*, which is not the same claim: once the budget is spent the queue drains at ~1/s, so a waiter's real wait is everyone ahead of it. The deadline now starts **before** the lock, so the 5 s bounds the call and not one sleep inside it. An **empty-but-well-formed 200 now persists as a real negative** — ETFs and most ADRs genuinely have no company profile, and without that they re-spent a quota slot on literally every load, forever. `signals/sector_breakdown.py`'s request path is now **cache-only and never touches the network**; misses are handed to a background fill paced at 1.2 s/symbol, so a cold symbol set completes in ~2 min and every load after is instant. **Result: 24 sectors, 0 unclassified, 1.5 s → 0.04 s.** Cache pre-filled for all 107 held symbols (106 resolved; the one miss is an ETF with no profile, correctly negative). The ticker panel and both `ai/research/data_sources` call sites inherit persistence + throttling for free. ⚠️ **Bug the fix exposed:** the new DB sits *outside* `DEFAULT_DB_PATH`, so `conftest.py`'s env-var isolation didn't cover it — `tests/test_finnhub_company.py` wrote a **mock Apple row** (`"logo": "https://logo"`) into the real `data/company_profiles.db`, and the next test in the same file read it back instead of its own mock. Exactly the hazard conftest's own header documents from two earlier occurrences; the lesson generalises past `TRADING_DB_PATH` — *any* new production DB path needs an isolation fixture the day it exists. Added autouse `_isolate_company_profile_cache`, deleted the poisoned row, re-fetched the real one. The same fixture also clears `_rate_calls` — the budget is module state, so enough mocked Finnhub tests inside one minute would spend the real budget and stall/refuse later tests for no reason of their own (a flake in the `ci-flake-shared-*` family, headed off rather than debugged later). | 2026-08-02 | **The reconciler can finally END a stuck execution row — and the probe that opened the round found a worse bug than the one it was sent for.** Two HANDOFF threads were open: nothing outside paper terminalised a stuck row, and `afetch_snapshot` is not atomic. **★ Checked the live broker BEFORE writing anything, and the check changed the round.** `AlpacaAdapter.aget_order_by_client_id` filtered `GET /v2/orders?client_order_ids=X` — and **Alpaca IGNORES that param entirely**: against the live paper API a total-garbage value returned the SAME four open orders as no filter at all, and the list defaults to `status=open` so any closed order is invisible. So the answer to "did MY order reach the broker?" was *whatever open order happened to be first* — typically a resting protective stop on another symbol. Three callers act on that answer as evidence about one specific order: the orphan sweep (**binds our execution row to a stranger's `broker_order_id`**, after which reconcile tracks someone else's order to decide our fill), `aplace_order`'s 409 recovery (returns a stranger's order as the placement — and `_parse_post_response` maps EVERY 422 to conflict, so an order never placed could be reported `submitted` against another order's id), and worst `_exit_may_be_live`, which decides whether a released protective stop goes back on: with any other resting order in the account it concluded "the exit is live" and left the position BARE; with none it concluded the opposite and would stack a stop on a live full-size sell. Fixed to the singular `GET /v2/orders:by_client_order_id`, verified live id-for-id on six real rows (closed orders resolve, a never-placed id returns clean `None`). No damage in the ledger: zero duplicate broker ids, zero submitted rows missing one. **Same family, same probe:** `get_open_orders` sent no `limit`, so it was silently capped at Alpaca's default 50 (`limit` IS honoured — measured); that list is where `pending_sell` comes from, so past 50 open orders in one account a resting sell vanishes and reads as free shares. Now asks the 500 maximum and logs loudly if it ever hits it. **The thread proper:** pending sweep no longer filters `execution_mode='paper'` (`submit` writes `pending` BEFORE it branches on mode, so a crash strands a row of any mode); the two branches that logged and `continue`d forever now recover via client id or end the row; `dry_run` short-circuits without a broker call. ★ **TWO Opus reviewers, split mandates — and BOTH landed.** Review B killed the second thread outright: reading positions AFTER orders looks like it buys an ordering invariant and does not (**measured ~21 ms of probability shift**, and Alpaca's fill→position lag is unmeasured), and worse, `_uncommitted_shares` carries a compensation (`held -= exit_qty`) that assumes positions is the OLDER read — making it the fresher one double-counts, zeroes the re-stop budget, and `_restop_residual` skips with `allot <= 0` and NO page: **an unprotected position plus an inbox note saying nothing was left uncommitted.** REVERTED, with a test pinning the concurrent read so the next attempt has to move both halves together. | 2026-08-02 | **A second sell inside one snapshot window can no longer oversell the position into an unintended short — and the adversarial review is what made it safe to ship.** Reproduced first: **12 shares sold against 10 held**, both `RiskEngine.validate` calls passing. `pending_sell` came SOLELY from `snapshot['open_orders']`, and a sell-to-close is not `exposure_increasing`, so that one figure was the ONLY quantity gate — while the snapshot refreshes on the poll loop but stays **valid for `_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE` = 5 MINUTES**, so the window is minutes, not the 20s poll. | 2026-07-29 | **Native chart candle fidelity — TWO unrelated bugs behind one founder report ("candles don't line up" + wick artifacts).** Founder reported wicks looking wrong and, separately, a gap appearing when a live intraday candle switched buckets. They turned out to be different layers, and the second is the one he actually meant — the first framing ("that's where the old bugs lived") was wrong and he correctly pushed back. **(1) Pixel geometry.** `series.ts` drew the body with `fillRect` (each edge independently `Math.round`ed) and the wick with `line` (`Math.floor(x·dpr)+0.5`) — body and wick snapped to *different* grids. Measured over 341 zoom levels: the wick sat ±0.5 device px off body centre and **flipped sides bar-to-bar at 81/169 spacings at dpr 1** (21/169 at dpr 2 — halved, never gone; a first-pass claim that it "disappears at dpr 2" was wrong and got retracted). `candleBodyWidth` rounded only the first term of `min(round(spacing·0.7), spacing−2)`, so below ~6.7px spacing the width went fractional (5.5 → 3.5) and rendered as **alternating 3px/4px bodies inside one frame** (70/341 zoom levels). Wick tips were left fractional in Y (`line` snaps only its CONSTANT axis) while body edges were snapped, so sub-pixel wicks smeared and the body's rounded edge half-ate them. Fix: one `Painter.barColumn(x, barSpacing)` primitive in the DOM adapter owns per-bar geometry — a single snapped centre shared by candle body, wick, volume bar and MACD histogram, with body width forced to the wick's **parity** (an even body has no middle column, so an odd wick must pick a side, and *which* side flips with frac(x) — that flip **was** the artifact; empirically, forcing odd width alone takes max lean 0.5 → 0). Width policy moved INTO the adapter because parity and the gap cap must be decided together: a first cut that snapped a 70% target to parity afterwards landed on the wick width and **erased the body across spacing 3.1–4.5**, and a second cut budgeted the gap against *average* slot width and let tight pairs touch (snapped centres sit floor/ceil(slot) apart, not slot) — both caught by the new tests, neither by eye. Wick now drawn as a `fillRect` so both ends snap and the span floors to a whole device px. Result, measured: lean 0.5 → **0** device px, multi-width frames 70/341 → **0**, zero touching bodies, default view byte-identical at a 5px body. Also `CanvasLayers.resize` pins the canvas CSS box to `bitmap/dpr` and `ChartEngine` rounds its logical size so `width·dpr` is whole — ResizeObserver hands out fractional boxes and a bitmap/box mismatch makes the browser resample the entire canvas, silently undoing every snap (**flagged, never confirmed live**; fixed unconditionally because it is 3 lines and correct either way). Accepted residuals: inter-candle gaps still alternate 1 device px (inherent to fractional bar spacing — TV lives with it too; removing it means quantizing zoom); at dpr 1, spacing 3.05–3.95 now renders bare wicks, since the only odd body that fits (3px in a 3.5px slot) would merge adjacent candles. **(2) The live-rollover phantom gap — the real complaint.** `native-chart.tsx` refetches every 30s (`INTRADAY_REFRESH_MS`) but the client bars-cache TTL is 60s on 1Min and **180s on 5Min**, so most refreshes were cache *hits*: `fetchBarsCached` returns the identical payload object, the component re-`.map()`ed it into a fresh array, and `setBars` replaced the engine's array wholesale — discarding every live tick merged since and, when the snapshot predated the current bucket, **deleting the forming candle outright**. The next WS tick (~100ms; quotes run at 10 Hz via `BROADCAST_THROTTLE_MS`) saw the tail one interval behind, rolled over again, and re-opened the candle at the *current* price — a gap the size of everything that moved since the snapshot (≤30s on 1m, ≤3min on 5m), i.e. "sometimes large, sometimes small" exactly as reported. Same family as `chart-stale-merge-fix` (07-06) but a DISTINCT mechanism: that was the ≥2-interval staleness gate fusing across a gap, this is a cache hit regressing the tail *inside* the freshness window. Fix: skip re-applying a payload object already applied (nothing to reconcile ⇒ leave the live bars alone), and otherwise reconcile through new pure `mergeFetchedBars(fetched, local)` in `chart-engine/merge.ts` — vendor bars always win, locally-rolled-over bars survive only strictly past the payload's last bar, so it can neither duplicate a timestamp nor reorder, and a stranded local bar drops as soon as the vendor publishes past it. 22 new tests (17 geometry invariants in `canvas2d.test.ts` across dpr 1/1.5/2 — wick centred, every edge on a whole device px, one body width per frame, bodies never touch; 5 merge-contract in `merge.test.ts`); 80 engine tests green, tsc + eslint clean on touched files (the 5 pre-existing `setState`-in-effect / ref-during-render errors in `native-chart.tsx` are outside the diff and were left alone). Built + deployed :3001 (BUILD_ID 17:09, MainPID 3140487, `/workspace` 200). **FOUNDER VERIFY:** watch a 1m/5m chart through several bucket switches — the gap should be gone; residual per-tick shimmer would be autoscale recomputing the price range every frame, a separate design question. **Not reviewed this round:** `equity-chart.tsx` / `pnl-chart.tsx` / `/charts` (Recharts, a wholly separate render path); futures 1H bars still bucket on UTC hours so a session's first hourly bar spans 30 min (equities use Alpaca native 1H, unaffected). |

| 2026-07-28 | **CI flake class RETIRED by measurement: the shared test-DB path, not "ambient daemons".** Three failures in one day (the post-#133 main push, a local full-suite run, PR #134's first CI) all showed `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: poll_runs` at random fixture setups, always green on re-run — and had been written off as runner-ambient noise. Root cause measured instead of assumed: `tests/conftest.py` pinned the throwaway DEFAULT_DB to a **fixed** path (`/tmp/hmt_pytest_default.db`) and deletes it at import; **serv is both the dev box and the self-hosted runner**, so any two overlapping pytest processes (local run + CI job, or two CI jobs) wipe each other's schema mid-run, and whichever test is mid-setup raises on a missing table. Volatility results do not transfer across frequencies: at 5-min the intraday U-shape dominates and neither plain EWMA nor plain GARCH models it, so an intraday verdict says more about time-of-day than about the estimators. Built the daily comparison properly instead: pulled ~10.5y of daily bars (Alpaca SIP back to 2016, 214k bars / 90 symbols — no leakage concern, neither estimator has a training corpus), walk-forward one-day-ahead from a 500-bar warmup on a 1000-bar rolling window, scored on **QLIKE** with a paired block-bootstrap CI **resampled over DATES** (every symbol moves with the market the same day — treating symbol-days as independent would badly understate the interval). **EWMA wins ties by rule** (`verdict()`): it's the zero-dependency incumbent, so GARCH is adopted only when it wins AND the whole 95% interval sits below zero. Perf: daily re-estimation would be ~194k fits (~4h) for no statistical gain since GARCH params barely move day to day — so re-estimate every 21 trading days and **filter the variance recursion forward daily** (`garch_forward`, the textbook σ²=ω+αr²+βσ²), the standard approach, ~15 min. `arch` stays an **on-demand research dep** installed into `.venv` but deliberately NOT in `requirements.txt` (the card scopes the arch dep out of the shipping path) — imported inside the functions so the CI suite never needs it; 7 tests, none importing arch. **RESULT — KEEP EWMA (deferral settled).** 85 symbols, **169,185 symbol-days**, 0 fit failures: GARCH QLIKE −6.7234 vs EWMA −6.7127, i.e. GARCH ahead by a mean of **0.0107** with 95% CI **[−0.0348, +0.0129] — straddling zero**. Under the pre-registered tie rule (EWMA wins ties), GARCH does **not** earn the `arch` dependency for daily sizing. Don't re-open without a NEW pre-registered question; a post-hoc regime slice hunting for a subset where GARCH wins is exactly the laundering the prereg exists to prevent. ⚠ **The first run returned EWMA QLIKE 4.4e10 — a bug, not a result**, and worth remembering as a class: NBIS (Nebius, ex-Yandex) was halted on Nasdaq ~2.5y, leaving 636 zero returns in 2,610 bars; a long run of identical closes decays EWMA variance to ~1e-9, so the first real post-halt move scores r²/σ² ≈ 1e17 and ONE symbol swamped 170k honest observations. GARCH looked fine only because its ω term structurally floors variance. Fixed with `is_degenerate()` (>20% zero returns ⇒ the instrument wasn't trading) + a 1bp `SIGMA_FLOOR`, **both applied identically to both arms** so the guard can't favour either. | 2026-06-25 | **CPU peg fixed — missing index on a poll-loop analytics query (101% → 2%).** A single core was pinned 24/7. Diagnosis took several wrong turns (the first instinct — "we re-fetch a year of bars every poll" — was wrong; verified daily `days=12` returns 8 bars not 252, and two speculative caches — sub-daily `bar_cache` + a short-TTL endpoint `response_cache` — moved CPU 0%, so both were reverted). A py-spy thread dump caught the real culprit: ONE thread spinning in `compute_and_save_snapshot_analytics` → `list_equity_history` (`db/sqlite.py`). That fires every 20s (poll loop, default account) and runs a 7-day equity JOIN of `poll_runs ⋈ account_snapshots`; `account_snapshots(poll_run_id)` had **no index**, so the JOIN was an O(n·m) nested-loop full-scan that grew with the DB — measured **43,623 ms** at 35k rows, overlapping every 20s into a permanent pool-saturating peg. Fix = one index: `idx_account_snapshots_poll_run ON account_snapshots(poll_run_id)` (+ `idx_position_snapshots_poll_run` for parity on the 86k-row table), added to `init_db` (idempotent, created on startup). Same query **43,623 ms → 18 ms (2,400×)**; live backend CPU **101.7% → 2.1%**. No `trading/` touch (snapshot/analytics read path only); 817 tests. **Lesson: profile before caching — every cache here was solving a non-problem; the bug was an unindexed FK join.** (The frontend's universe-sweep fetch storm the recon flagged is a separate, lower-priority I/O item, not the CPU peg.) |

| 2026-06-24 | **Live WS streaming actually works (dropped-tick root cause) + price-alert delivery + 10 Hz throttle — the three Mac/RN serv items.** Root cause found by a live-stream probe: the Schwab WS never streamed a single tick to clients — the phone always fell back to the ~6-12s REST crawl. The stream was connected and delivering ~1 tick/sec/symbol, but `SchwabMarketStreamHub._on_equity`/`_on_futures` read each tick's fields by the numeric enum `.value` (`LAST_PRICE.value`=3) while **schwab-py relabels every content dict to the field MEMBER NAME** (`"LAST_PRICE"`) before the handler runs (`_Handler.label_message`). So `item.get(3)` was always `None` → `price is None → continue` → **zero broadcasts, ever** (symbol came through the literal `"key"` field, so it looked "connected"). Fix: read by `.name` (`_EQ`/`_FUT` constants); verified against the LIVE stream (AAPL 297.38/+1.05%, NVDA 201.36, SPY 739.52 populate). **Streaming frame** now carries `ext_price`/`ext_change_pct`/`market_session` (`QuoteState` + `_quote_payload`); `BaseMarketHub.apply_extended()` lets the REST watchlist poll write ext-hours pricing through to the hub so every broadcast rides with it. **Price alerts** now broadcast FLAT (matching the rule-alert shape — was nested under `alert:{}`, which rendered blank on the phone) and ALSO fire an **APNs push** (`send_alert_push` gained a `data=` arg → flat `type:"price_alert"`/`symbol`/`alert_id` custom keys for tap-to-deep-link). **WS broadcast throttle** (`BROADCAST_THROTTLE_MS=100`): coalesces hot ticks to ~10 Hz/symbol/client (first tick immediate, further ticks collapse into one trailing send that re-reads state — latest price wins), alerts unthrottled — keeps the phone battery sane under Schwab's 30-100 ticks/sec. Also hardened the sync handler (deprecated `get_event_loop()` → `get_running_loop()` + `_inflight_ticks` hard-ref set so the GC can't cancel a broadcast mid-run). New tests: `tests/test_schwab_stream_handler.py` (4, labeled-key regression lock) + `tests/test_price_alert_dispatch.py` (5, flat alert + push + apply_extended + throttle). 725 tests, ruff + frontend typecheck clean. Mac/RN relay: `References/RN_STREAMING_ALERTS_RELAY.md`. ⚠️ Schwab allows ONE stream session per login — a local probe transiently kicks prod (reconnects ~2s). Schwab stays READ-ONLY. |
